profiles.meeting_scenario: A 30-minute coordination meeting between the model-adaptation lead and the hardware-mapping lead in an ML systems research group preparing the internal freeze for a paper on deploying BERT_Large-class models on a memristor-crossbar architecture using a large-small synergy design. The immediate context is a Monday internal review where they need one consistent set of tables and slides covering accuracy, area, and energy, plus a clean handoff between the model checkpoint/export artifacts and the crossbar mapping pipeline. The agenda is to confirm which artifact will be handed off, whether the shared results sheet is current, what should be included in the 'single-package' reporting numbers, and whether the work is considered ready for the review. The expected outcome is apparent alignment on interfaces and timing: M1 will stop model-side changes and update the text/figures, while M2 will refresh the hardware tables from the agreed artifact and place the final CSVs in the shared folder.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Senior Research Scientist, Efficient LLM Algorithms
members.expertise: LLM compression, calibration-aware export, evaluation pipelines for transformer deployment
members.background: Elena leads the model-side workstream that adapts BERT_Large-style transformers to the proposed memristor-friendly architecture and owns the accuracy tables used in the paper draft.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid reopening expensive evaluation runs and is mainly trying to preserve the current 'negligible accuracy loss' claim while making sure the hardware numbers reflect all deployment components reviewers might question.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the frozen checkpoint,' it refers to the export-ready artifact after her calibration pass, folded layer-normalization parameters, and routing annotations for the small helper modules.
Anything placed in the shared folder named 'bert_large_final' is implicitly the canonical artifact lineage for downstream hardware runs, so others will interpret it the same way she does.
The phrase 'single-package' naturally includes support SRAM and the small digital/nonlinear helper blocks that sit in the same deployment package, not just the memristor arrays themselves.
A result is effectively 'ready' once the headline accuracy and efficiency claims are stable enough for manuscript text, even if every seed or stress configuration has not been rerun.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.role: Research Engineer, Hardware Architecture and Mapping
members.expertise: Memristor crossbar mapping, package-level area/energy modeling, compiler and placement flows for transformer inference
members.background: Arjun owns the crossbar compiler, placement checks, and the area/energy spreadsheets that feed the systems-comparison tables in the paper.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the hardware pipeline stable, avoid retooling the mapper for last-minute export changes, and ensure the area/energy claims come from a reproducible placement run on his standard reporting path.
hidden_assumptions: When the model team says 'checkpoint,' they mean the pre-export weight state, because folding, scaling, and deployment-side transformations are supposed to happen consistently inside his compiler flow.

The shared document named 'bert_large_final' is anchored to the standard summary tab unless someone explicitly requests another configuration, so 'latest numbers' means the newest auto-generated summary there.

By default, 'single-package area/energy' means the crossbar tiles plus directly attached analog peripherals, while controller SRAM or auxiliary digital support is only added if someone explicitly asks for it.
A run is 'ready' once every layer places within capacity and the reporting scripts complete without errors on the current branch, even if model-side accuracy has not been re-aggregated.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the frozen checkpoint
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using 'the frozen checkpoint' for the final hardware run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the export-ready artifact after post-training calibration, parameter folding, and helper-module annotations have already been applied.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the pre-export model checkpoint, expecting his compiler to apply folding and scaling itself during mapping.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams routinely call their own handoff artifact a 'checkpoint,' and because the conversation is about coordination rather than redesign, the phrase feels precise enough on the surface.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest numbers' are in the shared results sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about pulling 'the latest numbers' from the shared 'bert_large_final' sheet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the long-context package-level tab updated after a recent reviewer-driven change to include the helper-path behavior.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the default summary tab auto-populated from the standard shorter-sequence mapping run generated earlier in the week.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is one shared document with a reassuringly final-sounding name, so saying 'latest numbers' sounds like ordinary coordination rather than something that needs tab- or config-level clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the single-package numbers
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the table should report 'single-package area and energy.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes the memristor arrays, peripheral circuits, support SRAM, and the small digital/nonlinear helper blocks because all of them are part of the claimed deployment package.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes the crossbar tiles and directly attached analog peripherals but not controller SRAM or auxiliary helper logic unless that inclusion is called out separately.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'single-package' sounds comprehensive and shared, but each person silently imports their own reporting convention from their subfield without realizing the boundary differs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the results should be 'ready for Monday' or 'sanity-checked by Monday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the headline table is stable enough to write around, with no meaningful drift from the approved accuracy claim, even if full reruns are deferred.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the placement and reporting pipeline completes cleanly with no capacity overflows or script failures, regardless of whether the model-side evaluation has been re-aggregated.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a busy pre-freeze coordination meeting, 'ready' is a socially smooth status word that signals progress, so each person hears confirmation of their own completion standard.
